title: Jameis Winston benched: J.J. McCarthy sparks Giants, but thrilling, historic comeback falls just short - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy helped New York score 17 unanswered points before ultimately coming up just short
body:
McCarthy helped New York score 17 unanswered points before ultimately coming up just short
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It could be the beginning of a new era in New York, as the Giants benched quarterback Jameis Winston for J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter of their eventual 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. While McCarthy threw an interception on his third passing attempt, he rebounded to spark the Giants and made his case to be John Harbaugh's new starter.In all, McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception in his first extensive action with his new team. In 11 minutes of action, he would throw for 243 yards, which made NFL history for the most passing yards in an 11-minute span. He also led the Giants in rushing with 26 yards. Following his interception, McCarthy led a six-play, 52-yard drive that was capped by a Tyrone Tracy Jr. touchdown and a successful Isaiah Likely two-point conversion to trim the deficit to 16 points. After a Saints three-and-out, McCarthy took the Giants offense 73 yards down the field on just three plays, and hit Likely for a 24-yard touchdown to make it a 10-point game. 
McCarthy was given the opportunity to lead a game-tying or game-winning drive with 57 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter with zero timeouts. On first down, he scrambled up the middle for 28 yards to get the Giants into enemy territory, and then hit Likely for 20 yards to get New York to the Saints' 23-yard line. The Giants eventually faced a fourth-and-1 14 yards from the end zone with 12 seconds remaining, and McCarthy could not connect with Likely in the end zone. The Giants wanted a flag on this play, but the officials held onto their yellow handkerchiefs. 
This was a performance good enough for McCarthy to unseat Winston permanently. Last month, the Giants traded a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for McCarthy. The former No. 10 overall pick went 6-4 as the starter for the Vikings in 2025, completing 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He became the only first-round pick at quarterback since 1970 to finish last in completion percentage and TD-INT ratio in their debut season. 
Harbaugh said after the game he can't answer who his starting quarterback will be moving forward, and that those are not issues decided 10 minutes after a game. 
It's called the "Jameis Winston experience" for a reason. Last week in the tie vs. the Washington Commanders, he completed 33 of 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns. Winston actually became the first Giants quarterback to throw three touchdowns in back-to-back games since Eli Manning in 2016. However, his performance on Sunday opened the door for Harbaugh to consider his other quarterback. Winston completed 14 of 26 passes for 152 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions before his benching.

schema.headline: Jameis Winston benched: J.J. McCarthy sparks Giants, but thrilling, historic comeback falls just short - CBS Sports

title: College football odds, lines, schedule for Week 8: Texas favored vs. Ole Miss - CBS Sports
description: Initial odds for college football's top Week 8 matchups are out
body:
Initial odds for college football's top Week 8 matchups are out
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two weeks away from the first set of College Football Playoff rankings coming out of the wildest Saturday across the sport in decades, the 2026 season has delivered in a big way so far.For the first time in the 90-year history of the AP poll dating back to 1936, five of the top seven teams lost on the same afternoon, sparking a much-needed rebound opportunity for the perceived elites in Week 8. While next weekend's matchups within the top 25 fail to offer a litany of "good on good" games like last, the unpredictability of the sport this season continues to carry significant weight.The only unbeatens remaining at midseason are BYU, James Madison, Miami, Texas Tech, UCLA and Utah after most of the unblemished went down on Saturday. Could more fall in Week 8 to unranked foes?Let's take a look at the schedule and early lines.Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook.
The big gamesNo. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas (-3.5): Will the Longhorns rebound as a home favorite against the Rebels, or will Steve Sarkisian lose a third straight SEC game and bring more questions to the Forty Acres this season? It benefits Texas if defensive end Colin Simmons, who leads the country with 10.5 sacks, returns after being carted off against Florida, but his injury status remains unknown. Trinidad Chambliss is the SEC's top individual playmaker at quarterback and has already had his way against two nationally-ranked opponents this fall with impressive wins over LSU and Missouri.No. 6 Indiana (-7.5) at Michigan: Backup quarterback Tommy Carr provided an immediate spark for the Wolverines against Penn State, leading multiple second-half touchdown drives after being plucked from the bench ahead of Bryce Underwood. Manufacturing that same level of success against the defending national champions, who saw their nation-leading 22-game winning streak snapped vs. Ohio State, is a different task entirely. Indiana hasn't won at Michigan Stadium since 1967, which is perhaps why this opening line seems a bit on the low side.No. 11 Tennessee (-2.5) at South Carolina: Can Shane Beamer knock off another top-15 SEC opponent with the Gamecocks? He's had an extra week to prepare -- 3-4 overall at South Carolina in that spot -- for what the Vols bring to Williams-Brice Stadium in a pivotal matchup for Tennessee's lasting CFP hopes. The Gamecocks clicked for the first time all season offensively last time out at Florida after LaNorris Sellers accounted for five total touchdowns. These two have split their last eight meetings dating back to 2016.No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah (-5.5): The Utes survived a Big 12 warning shot at Colorado on Saturday night and now get a red-hot Cougars squad hoping to occupy one of the conference's multiple seats at the CFP table. Houston held off Oklahoma State, 35-32, in Week 7 behind Conner Weigman's five touchdown passes. For Utah, protecting home turf means preserving its unbeaten record and strengthening a playoff résumé that needs its first quality win with BYU looming on Nov. 7.
No. 18 LSU (-6.5) at Auburn: Alex Golesh and the Tigers just knocked the SEC's king off the throne and now comes the tricky part: doing it again at home with everyone paying closer attention. LSU's coming off a 31-point demolition of Mississippi State and knows the margin for error is near zero the rest of the way in SEC play. Was Auburn's win between the hedges a turning point for the program or this season's signature moment? We'll know more after Week 8 inside Jordan-Hare.Best of the restPittsburgh at No. 1 Miami (-22.5)Texas A&M at No. 13 Alabama (-15.5)No. 2 BYU (-7.5) at UCFNo. 8 Texas Tech (-11.5) at CincinnatiMichigan State at No. 9 UCLA (-12.5)Vanderbilt at No. 12 Kentucky (-11.5)Oklahoma (-2.5) at Mississippi StateNo. 15 Iowa (-5.5) at MinnesotaColorado at Oklahoma State (-13.5)No. 16 USC (-2.5) at WisconsinNo. 21 Boise State (-13.5) at Washington StateCalifornia at No. 23 SMU (-17.5)Rutgers at No. 24 Northwestern (-15.5)

title: Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy suffers injury during Steelers' game vs. Buccaneers - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy spent halftime in the blue medical tent
body:
McCarthy spent halftime in the blue medical tent
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Instead of spending halftime in the locker room, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy spent it in the medical tent after he sustained an ankle injury at the conclusion of the first half.McCarthy was starting to make his way to the locker room when he started limping and had trouble walking. He was then assisted off the field and into the blue medical tent. He did not speak to the Steelers at halftime.After the game, he revealed he had been stepped on, and that's why he had to go into the blue tent. However, he said he is feeling better. He told the media he delegated much of the halftime head coach responsibilities to assistant coach Joe Whitt Jr. Despite the injury, McCarthy returned to the sideline for the start of the second half. He has also resumed his duties as the team's offensive playcaller. According to the CBS Sports broadcast team, McCarthy twisted his ankle, but it's unclear exactly when or what caused it. 
McCarthy's injury capped off what was a lousy first half for the Steelers, who trailed 13-3 at the intermission. Pittsburgh committed several mental errors in the first half, including Darnell Washington's juggling of an Aaron Rodgers pass, which was ultimately picked off by A'Shawn Robinson. The pick set up the game's first score, a 43-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin. The Steelers' offense gained just 102 yards in the first half. They were just 1-of-6 on third down and 0-of-1 on fourth down. Jalon Daniels, the Buccaneers' undrafted rookie quarterback, dominated the Steelers in the first 30 minutes. Daniels completed nine consecutive passes at one point and recorded the game's first touchdown on a short touchdown pass to Emeka Egbuka. 
The Steelers went on to beat the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime.

schema.headline: Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy suffers injury during Steelers' game vs. Buccaneers - CBS Sports

title: NFL Week 6 overreactions: Time for Colts to clean house? A.J. Brown trade a mistake by Patriots? - CBS Sports
description: The battle between two of the NFL's most woebegone franchises lived up to its lack of hype Sunday. In fact, in terms of excitement, it m
body:
The battle between two of the NFL's most woebegone franchises lived up to its lack of hype Sunday. In fact, in terms of excitement, it more than lived up to it. But the on-field product was a special sort of fun-bad.Titans 26, Colts 20. It's the first win of the year for Tennessee, and a stunning one at that. The Titans trailed 13-0 at halftime and looked completely lifeless. Bench Cam Ward? Throw in the towel? It seemed on the brink.And then the Colts, being the generous team they are, quite literally gave it away over the next four possessions:Jonathan Taylor fumbled on the first play of the second half. The Titans turned that into a field goal.With the Colts in scoring range on the next drive, Daniel Jones threw an atrocious interception. The Titans turned that into another field goal.The Colts then went three-and-out and gave up a 58-yard Chimere Dike return, setting up the Titans for their lone offensive touchdown of the day.On the next drive, Julius Chestnut blocked a punt, and Oluwafemi Oladejo recovered the loose ball and scored a touchdown.From up 13-0 to down 20-13 in about 18 minutes of game time. Horrifying stuff. The Colts actually tied the game on a Taylor touchdown, only for the defense to commit an awful pass interference to set up a Titans field goal. Tennessee tacked on another field goal late.
A collapse in all three stages? Against a winless team? For an organization already skating on thin ice? Check, check, check. Which leads me to say ...Shane Steichen won't last the season, and Chris Ballard and Daniel Jones will be gone between now and Week 1, 2027Overreaction or reality: RealitySince 2020, there have been 16 in-season coaching changes. Shane Steichen will either be the next or, at the very least, join that list.This was an unacceptable collapse. The Titans are completely inept offensively. The only way they could do anything was if the Colts blew it, and the Colts blew it over and over again. I've generally been a proponent of Steichen as a good offensive mind, but as a head coach, you have to be more than that. You are responsible for everything, and in that matter, Indianapolis isn't close to good enough.
Steichen can't play the game, though, so we turn to the players ... and the person who chose them. Chris Ballard is in his 10th season as Colts GM. The team has one playoff win over that span, and it was back in 2018, his second year. He has been completely unable to find a quarterback, and his latest attempt is turning out as bad as the others.Remember, at the start of Ballard's tenure, he had Andrew Luck. Andrew Luck retired ahead of the 2019 season. It's been that long. Inexcusable. He has tried half-measures with veterans. He tried drafting one (Anthony Richardson). He has failed in every measure. The defense remains iffy at best, even after the blockbuster (and, in retrospect, misjudged) Sauce Gardner trade.But really, it all comes back to Jones: He was 22-for-42 for 269 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. He took six sacks. He's tied for the NFL lead in turnovers. Sunday, he simply did not put an NFL-caliber product on the field.
Remember, the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million deal over the offseason, even though they were bidding with ... no one. There is an out after this year that would carry $35 million in dead cap, but continuing with him would be even more punitive for a franchise long overdue for a reset.Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is known for standing on the sideline and keeping notes. Her only notes needed from Sunday? It's time to clean house.The Browns or Steelers will win the AFC NorthOverreaction or reality: OverreactionWell, well, well, if it isn't a three-way tie atop the AFC North through six weeks?! The Browns, Steelers and Ravens are all 4-2, and the Bengals (on bye this weekend) aren't far behind at 3-2.
Cleveland technically leads the division thanks to Sunday's 13-10 win over Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore, and Pittsburgh is second because it has a better in-division record.Sorry, Browns and Steelers fans, but neither one of you is winning the division. Cleveland's largest win this season is by four points. It lost to the Jets just last week. Deshaun Watson looked awful Sunday. The Steelers looked similarly awful, needing a late comeback to force overtime against the Baker Mayfield-less Buccaneers. As it turns out, playing against backup quarterbacks is very helpful.Both teams rank in the bottom half of most major offensive stats. The quarterback play simply isn't good enough and won't be good enough, especially when put up against Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow rather than Tyler Huntley and Jalon Daniels.
Patriots made a mistake trading for A.J. BrownOverreaction or reality: OverreactionA.J. Brown's grand return from IR was ... not so grand. Three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets. Officially, he's been charged with two drops. Unofficially, given his high standards, it was probably more. He even bobbled away a Jets onside kick, but lucky for him, a teammate recovered to clinch the Patriots' 26-19 win.It's worth being concerned about the debut, but to say the trade is a bust or a mistake would be a drastic overreaction. Yes, it's been a tough start with the injury and the underwhelming return. But let's not write it off. He won on the routes New England brought him in to win: quick in-breakers and deep balls. Drake Maye missed him on one of each, and Brown failed to finish other opportunities he did have. It sounds like a silly thing to say, but if you cut the tape right before the ball arrives, Brown's film would look encouraging.Of course, he has to make the plays that are there. Getting open doesn't gain yards, score points or win games. Brown will bounce back, and he can still be a huge boost. He came back from his high ankle sprain earlier than expected. Let's give him a week's worth of grace.
C.J. Stroud will be a top-five highest-paid quarterback this offseason ... and deserves itOverreaction or reality: RealityAnother week, another outstanding performance for C.J. Stroud. The fourth-year pro threw for 312 yards, three touchdowns and an interception and led the game-winning drive in the Texans' 34-31 win over the Jaguars.The numbers are one thing, but the film is just as good, if not better. This is one of the best throws you will see all season.
So is this one ...
This is Stroud at his best: laser-accurate, huge arm, can access every part of the field. It's been missed the past few years, and the Texans should be very glad it's back. Not only that, but he is improving at mitigating negative plays. His interception Sunday was really bad, but it was his first all year. He's also taking fewer devastating sacks than he did last season. And he's doing it all while still not having much of a run game.
The Texans and Stroud didn't reach an extension in the offseason. He had been awful in the playoffs, and while both sides said the right things, no agreement happened.He is very much on the way to earning that massive extension this offseason, though. This offseason is setting up to be a huge one for quarterback deals — Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye and Bo Nix from the 2024 class, Bryce Young from Stroud's 2023 class and Lamar Jackson are all looking for a new deal. Stroud's deal will put him among the top five highest-paid quarterbacks, and it will be well-deserved.Brad Idzik will be a hot head-coaching candidate in 2027Overreaction or reality: RealityThe Panthers topped the injury-battered Eagles 25-14 in straightforward fashion. Bryce Young threw a pair of touchdown passes, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score. Philadelphia was without Jalen Hurts, its top three running backs and a bunch of other players. It's not a super notable result by any measure.
But Philadelphia still has a really good defense, and Brad Idzik flashed excellent play calling, including on both touchdowns to Tommy Tremble.
I was also super impressed by Young's work on RPO throws, something Idzik and Young have worked into this offense really well.Idzik took over calling plays from Dave Canales this offseason. It has been a perfect promotion. Carolina has one of the most aggressive offenses in the NFL in terms of passing rates. It's a really well-designed offense that empowers Young and accentuates his strengths. In an NFL that loves young, innovative play callers, Idzik is part of the next wave of hotshots.

schema.headline: NFL Week 6 overreactions: Time for Colts to clean house? A.J. Brown trade a mistake by Patriots? - CBS Sports

title: Rams kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return after suffering knee injury minutes into L.A. debut - CBS Sports
description: Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kicko
body:
Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Los Angeles Rams' kicking conundrum continues into Week 6, but not in the way you'd expect. After cutting former placekicker Harrison Mevis after Week 5, L.A. seemingly found its solution after signing veteran Blake Grupe to assume the kicking duties. The former Notre Dame kicker made his Rams debut on Sunday and quickly endeared himself to his new squad by netting a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter. However, things went downhill after that. Grupe is now doubtful to return to Sunday's contest due to a knee injury, the team announced. Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on the kickoff following his made field goal. He was seen lowering his shoulder to hit returner Devin Duvernay and came down awkwardly. 
With Grupe sidelined, the entire kicking operation is reshuffled. Punter Ethan Evans will serve as the kicker, while receiver Jordan Whittington could be the holder, as ESPN notes he was working on holds along the sideline. Grupe entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2023, initially signing with the Saints. He played for New Orleans until midway through the 2025 season, when he was released. After that, he made stops with the Colts and Jets before finding his way to the Rams. Coming into this game, Grupe had converted 81.9% of his career field goals (86-of-105) and 98% of his extra points (96-of-98). 
The kicking game has been an issue throughout the first half of the season for the Rams, and it came to a head during Monday's overtime loss to the Bills. Mevis failed to convert on either of his field goal attempts, including what would've been a game-winner, which was blocked. That forced Los Angeles' hand to make a change in favor of Grupe, but this latest injury keeps them in a kicking nightmare.

schema.headline: Rams kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return after suffering knee injury minutes into L.A. debut - CBS Sports

title: Maryland fires DC Ted Monachino: Mike Locksley's future remains in doubt - CBS Sports
description: After a 2-5 start and another defensive collapse, Locksley made a change entering Maryland's bye week in hopes of
body:
After a 2-5 start and another defensive collapse, Locksley made a change entering Maryland's bye week in hopes of turning the season -- and his trajectory -- around
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Maryland fired defensive coordinator Ted Monachino on Sunday after the defense struggled again in the Terrapins' 37-30 loss to Rutgers.Maryland's defense hasn't lived up to expectations in what has been a disappointing 2-5 start to the Terrapins' 2026 campaign. Maryland currently ranks 83rd in total defense, 84th in pass defense, 85th in rush defense and 127th in scoring defense. "I appreciate Ted's hard work and dedication to our program during his time in College Park," Maryland coach Mike Locksley said. "As I evaluate our program, I believe this change is necessary. We wish Ted all the best moving forward."The decision comes as Locksley's long-term job status is also very much in doubt. After going 4-8 in 2024 and 2025, Locksley entered the 2026 season needing to win around seven games or better to keep his job headed into 2027. Following another blown opportunity against Rutgers on Saturday, the odds of that happening have plummeted. Locksley hasn't beaten a Power Four opponent in more than a calendar year and has a 2-20 Big Ten conference record since the 2024 season. 
There may not be a coach on a hotter seat in college football than Locksley. While there has been considerable outside speculation on Locksley's job security, including whether he'd be fired headed into the open week, Maryland has taken a patient approach in evaluating the situation. Letting Locksley fire Monachino to try to improve the defense headed into a bye week is another example of that. Monachino had been Maryland's defensive coordinator the last two seasons after arriving from North Carolina. The veteran defensive coach had also previously worked for the Baltimore Ravens, Indianapolis Colts, Atlanta Falcons and Jacksonville Jaguars. Co-defensive coordinator Aazaar Abdul-Rahim will take over defensive play-calling responsibilities as Maryland's interim defensive coordinator. Abdul-Rahim, who coaches the cornerbacks, is on his second stint at Maryland after previously working for D.J. Durkin. Inside linebackers coach Zac Spatival will also add the co-defensive coordinator title. 
Maryland has a bye this week before a Halloween home game against Illinois.

schema.headline: Maryland fires DC Ted Monachino: Mike Locksley's future remains in doubt - CBS Sports

title: NFL, Saints address plans for Paris game during Week 6 as protests escalate in France - CBS Sports
description: The league says its continuing with its original plans and monitoring the situation
body:
The league says its continuing with its original plans and monitoring the situation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Protests escalated in France over the weekend over living costs and education, raising concerns over the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints scheduled to take place in Paris next week. The unrest stems in part from citizens demanding better school conditions, teacher shortages and public services, but it has since grown as violent groups have rioted, clashed with police, and set fire to public buildings. At least 1,800 across the country, according to CBS News. Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets across the nation to demand change from the government, as both protesters and law enforcement have turned to violent methods. Concern over player, personnel, and fan safety has become the main topic surrounding next week's international game, the first-ever regular-season matchup to take place in France.The league released a statement last week saying they still plan to conduct the game as scheduled on Oct. 25 and provided a similar update on Sunday after news of the social unrest spread."Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said. "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
Saints executive Greg Bensel backed the league's statement and offered some insight into the league's safety precautions. "We concur with the NFL's statement and are planning to play the game. In addition to working closely with the NFL, we have also maintained daily security updates with our security partners in France," Bensel said. "Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites."Last week, the league's statement said, "We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25. As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."
The game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET, 2:30 p.m. local time. The Saints are scheduled to leave Sunday night and spend the week practicing in France.The league has changed games in the past due to various factors, including weather and field conditions, so it is not entirely out of the realm of possibility that the game could be moved. The Saints are considered the home team, so if they did move it, which they clearly do not plan to do right now, New Orleans would be the obvious new location.While protests have taken over Paris, it's not the only place in France affected. Here's more from CBS News:
"Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities."In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate told LCI television that the fire was deliberately set and nearly destroyed the building. The fire was under control Sunday.""Around Paris' Place de la République on Sunday morning, dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass marked the aftermath of the events. Looting and damage were reported around the square and in some other tourist and shopping areas in the city center."Paris police said Sunday that 855 people were arrested in the French capital region alone. The Paris prosecutors' office said that 557 of them were kept in police custody."

schema.headline: NFL, Saints address plans for Paris game during Week 6 as protests escalate in France - CBS Sports

title: Eagles lose another starter to injury after team already without Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, others - CBS Sports
description: Nolan Smith exited with a concussion and will not return
body:
Nolan Smith exited with a concussion and will not return
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Eagles EDGE Nolan Smith Jr. suffered a concussion in the first half of Philadelphia's game against the Panthers and will not return, the team announced. Smith took a hard hit to the head when Carolina running back Chuba Hubbard came over to chip block him.
It's yet another injury for a team that can ill afford to lose pretty much anyone at any position. The Eagles came into Sunday's matchup already missing ...quarterback Jalen Hurts, who landed on IR this week with a superficial blood clotrunning back Saquon Barkley, who is missing his second straight game with a hamstring injuryrunning back Tank Bigsby, who landed on IR after core muscle surgeryrunning back Will Shipley, who suffered a foot injury last weekguard Landon Dickerson, who landed on IR with a knee injury in Week 1... on offense.Specifically speaking to Smith's injury, the Eagles are down to three edge rushers with Smith out. A.J. Epenesa (back) and Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) are both out this week, leaving Jonathan Greenard (who has been bothered by pec and ankle injuries this year), Arnold Ebiketie and Keyshawn James-Newby.Smith, a 2023 first-round pick, entered the game with two sacks this year and added his third early in the game.
The Eagles (2-3) trailed 10-7 at halftime and are trying to avoid their fourth straight loss.

schema.headline: Eagles lose another starter to injury after team already without Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, others - CBS Sports

title: NFL addresses safety concerns for Steelers-Saints game in France protests in Paris continues - CBS Sports
description: The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
body:
The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With protests on their third week in Paris and an NFL game scheduled to take place in the city in just a week, growing concern over fan and player safety has left some wondering if the league will alter any of its plans. But the NFL said on Wednesday that the game will go on as scheduled, with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meeting on Oct. 25 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, located just north of Paris."We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25," the NFL said in a statement earlier this week, via ESPN. "As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."As protests continue, the league released another statement emphasizing that they plan to play the game in Paris."Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said. "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
The social unrest stems from demands for the government to change multiple aspects of the education system. Protestors are asking the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. Students say the schools are falling apart and rats are in the buildings. The protests have sparked violence, with authorities using tear gas, stun grenades and various other means to attempt to stop the crowds. Protestors have reportedly set fires and caused damage. Police detained over 5,000 people in connection with protests, according to CBS News. Local officials say they are investigating both the protests and the police response. 
The French government is currently in a "political deadlock" as they approach the presidential elections in the spring. They have not responded to protestors with any plans or solutions for their complaints and demands. If the situation in Paris escalates, the NFL could reconsider its stance, but right now, it is sticking with its original plan. The NFL has changed game locations in the past due to extreme weather or field conditions. The Saints are considered the home team for the game, and their only listed event for the day in New Orleans is a private event where youth and amateur sports teams have the chance to play inside the stadium. It is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. local time, so if needed, the game could seemingly be played at Caesar's Superdome. But that seems unlikely at the moment.
If the game does go on as planned, it will mark the first-ever NFL game played in France.  This will be the second straight year the Steelers play a game outside the United States, having played in Dublin last season against the Minnesota Vikings. The Saints last played an international game in 2022, visiting London to face the Vikings.

schema.headline: NFL addresses safety concerns for Steelers-Saints game in France protests in Paris continues - CBS Sports

title: Jaguars' Travis Hunter breaks out vs. Texans; showcases long-term, two-way potential for Jacksonville - CBS Sports
description: Hunter is hitting his stride with his utilization in 2026, making history with an interception and a receiving to
body:
Hunter is hitting his stride with his utilization in 2026, making history with an interception and a receiving touchdown in Week 6
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Second-year CB/WR Travis Hunter showcased the tantalizing two-way production on Sunday that the Jacksonville Jaguars dreamed about when they traded up to select the 2024 Heisman Trophy winner second overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. Jacksonville traded the 2025 fifth overall pick, a 2025 second-round pick (No. 36), a 2025 fourth-round pick (No. 126) and a 2026 first-round pick to the Cleveland Browns to move up three spots to the second overall pick while also picking up a 2025 fourth-round pick (No. 104) and a 2025 sixth-round pick (No. 200). That was a heavy investment of draft capital for Hunter, and the Jaguars weren't able to fully capitalize on his skillset his rookie year with it being cut short at the end of October by a torn LCL. The Jaguars fell 34-31 after a buzzer-beating field goal from the Houston Texans in London. But the game represented the start of the game-changing, two-way impact they envisioned for Hunter. He started at cornerback while catching all four of his targets at wide receiver for 59 yards and a touchdown, a seven-yarder that cut the Texans' lead to 31-28 with 11:26 left in the game. On the next Texans' drive after his touchdown, Hunter picked off Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud in the end zone for a crucial stop, marking Stroud's first interception of the entire 2026 season. That allowed the Jaguars to tie the game at 31 with 1:55 left to play. Hunter is now the first player with a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game since Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Dawkins did so back in 2022, also against the Texans. Hunter's performance on Sunday is now just the fourth time a player has produced a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game (including the playoffs) since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. 
Receiving TD and INT in same game( including playoffs), since 1970 AFL/NFL mergerOpponentJAX Travis Hunter (2026)HOUPHI Brian Dawkins (2002)HOUNYJ Keyshawn Johnson (1998)*JAXSTL Roy Green (1981)WAS* Occurred in the playoffsHow Hunter is being deployedIt's interesting to see the shift in how the Jaguars are deploying Hunter this season compared to his rookie year in 2025. Last season, Hunter profiled as a full-time wide receiver moonlighting at cornerback. Of his 459 total snaps from scrimmage, around two-thirds of them were on offense (66.4%, 305 of 459) and a third of them were on defense (33.6%, 154 of 459) in seven games played. He racked up 298 yards receiving and a touchdown with 28 catches on 45 targets while totaling three passes defended and a fumble with 15 total tackles in seven games in 2025.So far in 2026, Hunter has transitioned to full-time cornerback while playing wide receiver as a side hustle. Of his 322 snaps from scrimmage this season, just over 90% of them (90.7%, 292 of 322) are on defense, and just under 10% of them (9.3%, 30 of 322) are on offense. Hunter has caught all six of his targets this season for 76 yards receiving and a touchdown, with the bulk of that coming on Sunday. He's also totaled two interceptions, three passes defended, and 22 tackles in six games. 
It seems like head coach Liam Coen and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile have found a winning formula for Hunter's usage with the team out to a 4-2 start and first place in the AFC South through six weeks. More often than not, Hunter making a splash on both sides of the ball will yield winning outcomes for the Jaguars, exactly what Jacksonville hoped for when trading up to select him second overall just two drafts ago.

title: Cam Skattebo demotion: Giants RB logs zero touches, responds to apparent benching - CBS Sports
description: After a slew of fumbling mistakes, Skattebo has lost his starting job to Najee Harris
body:
After a slew of fumbling mistakes, Skattebo has lost his starting job to Najee Harris
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the wake of an array of fumbles this season, Cam Skattebo was completely phased out of the New York Giants offense in Week 6. Coming into Sunday's action, a report from ESPN noted there would be a change in the New York backfield rotation. Najee Harris was likely to see a large role, while Skattebo was downgraded. The assumption was that even amid a demotion, Skattebo would be in the mix of the Giants' rushing attack. However, that never came to fruition during the club's 34-27 loss to New Orleans. Skattebo did not log a single carry or a single target on Sunday. This marked the first time in his career that Skattebo was active for a game but did not see any touches. In all, Skattebo played six snaps. "I didn't expect to have zero," Skattebo said after the game, via The Athletic. "I was expecting to not play as much just like I did. The message was to keep your head down and keep going. They understand the type of player I am, and I just got to continue doing my job and do it to the best of my ability.  
Postgame, head coach John Harbaugh said Skattebo's lack of action "wasn't by design" and that he was not benched. "It was not by design for him not to carry the ball," he said, via Yahoo Sports. "When he was in there, we didn't call any runs. You're not thinking about which back is in the game and how many runs they're getting."
With Skattebo on the outside looking in on the rushing attack, the Giants finished the day with 20 carries for 84 yards (4.2 yards per carry average) and one touchdown. Specifically, Giants backs rushed 14 times for 34 yards and a touchdown. Tyrone Tracy Jr. led the way with six carries, followed by Devin Singletary and Najee Harris, who each finished with four attempts. 
On top of the carries, Tracy saw three targets (two catches), while Singletary was targeted once (one catch). Skattebo's demotion stems from fumbling issues. So far this season, he's fumbled four times, including a back-breaking fumble last week in the overtime tie to the Washington Commanders. That turnover at the Washington 24-yard line eliminated an opportunity for a game-winning kick and instead led to the Giants nearly losing the contest had it not been for Jayden Daniels and the Commanders' offense mismanaging the clock en route to the tie. "I got punished for what I did (last week)," Skattebo said. "I understand it, so I gotta be ready when coach calls my name, and that wasn't today."
He later added: "It's hard, but I've made mistakes, and I got to own up to them. If that is what they want to do -- keep me on the sidelines because of that -- I totally understand."New York will be in Houston next Sunday for a Week 7 matchup against the Texans before entering the bye in Week 8.

title: AP Top 25: Miami new No. 1, BYU to No. 2; Texas slides in college football rankings - CBS Sports
description: There is a change at the top for the second straight week amid a chaotic weekend of upsets, while BYU's win over
body:
There is a change at the top for the second straight week amid a chaotic weekend of upsets, while BYU's win over Notre Dame earned major respect from the voters
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The wildest Saturday in college football history led to a significant shakeup in the weekly Associated Press Top 25 poll.When five of the eight top-ranked teams all lost on the same day -- the first time in AP poll history -- it guaranteed a new-look top 10. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes are the new No. 1 team in the country, receiving 40 first-place votes. The Hurricanes, atop the AP poll for the first time since 2002, jumped last week's No. 1 Georgia, which slipped to No. 5 after a last-second home loss to unranked Auburn. The Big 12 was the biggest benefactor from Saturday's chaos atop the rankings. BYU jumped all the way up to No. 2 after its controversial win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame. The Fighting Irish fell two spots to No. 4 despite the Big 12 issuing a statement afterward that officials erred in not putting another second on the clock. Texas Tech jumped up two spots to No. 8 after its blowout win over Arizona State. 
The Big 12 now has a conference-best three top-10 teams. The Big Ten also has three top-10 teams (Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA), while the SEC has two. 
        
            
                College football's ranked-win leaders: Teams with the most victories vs. current AP Top 25
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
SEC already eating itselfA week ago, the SEC had four teams in the top 10 and seven in the top 15. This week: Two in the top 10 and five in the top 15. It's no surprise that the SEC is beating itself up, though seeing the Big 12 with more top 10 teams is admittedly eye-opening. The SEC slate is always challenging, and moving to a nine-game conference schedule naturally made it tougher. But Saturday showed just how challenging from top-to-bottom the SEC is this season. The only top-10 team from last week to survive unscathed was Ole Miss. Georgia, Texas and Alabama all went down on Saturday, with two of those losses coming at home. There is no longer an unbeaten team in the SEC, and it sure looks likely there will be more chaos to come within the conference. 
First-year success at UCLA, KentuckyUCLA is a top 10 team. Kentucky is the No. 12 team.In football. Seriously.UCLA's Bob Chesney and Kentucky's Will Stein should be the co-frontrunners for Coach of the Year awards for what they've already accomplished in just half a season. Chesney took over a program that went 3-9 last season and fired head coach DeShaun Foster after only three games. The No. 9 Bruins are 6-0 and ranked in the top 10 for the first time since 2022. UCLA's 17-7 win over Wisconsin without quarterback Nico Iamaleava showed that this team is a legitimate College Football Playoff contender. Stein's situation was a bit better -- the Wildcats went 5-7 in Mark Stoops' last season -- but to be 6-1 in the SEC with wins over LSU, Oklahoma and Texas A&M is beyond impressive. title: Premier League Power Rankings: Brighton continue to impress, Aston Villa surge - CBS Sports
description: Brighton and Hove Albion's 5-0 win over Crystal Palace was the highlight of the weekend, ensuring the Seagulls re
body:
Brighton and Hove Albion's 5-0 win over Crystal Palace was the highlight of the weekend, ensuring the Seagulls remain this season's pleasant surprise for another week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Seven weeks into the Premier League season, teams are starting to sort themselves into groups and one thing is starting to become very clear – there are more average-to-poor teams than usual, the collection of them continuing to bounce around the table even as preseason rust becomes a thing of the past.Manchester City, who are in first place despite the cloud of their financial breaches, and Arsenal remain the cream of the crop while Brighton and Hove Albion are the unexpectedly exciting side of the season thus far. Liverpool and Chelsea feel a step behind but still feel on course for strong campaigns. Every other team feels somewhat flawed, in some ways notably unspectacular but the places on the table need to be filled by someone and so a number of teams currently find themselves in surprising spots. The surprises are not always good ones, though, depending on the team in question.Some are doing their best to claw themselves out of the surprisingly bad circumstances they find themselves in, Bournemouth and Fulham each picking up their first wins of the season this weekend while Aston Villa added another to their tally after a poor start. Brighton, meanwhile, are joined by Leeds United in finding themselves further up the table than some might expect. The early season confusion in the standings has not dissipated just yet, though, resulting in another fascinating batch of power rankings.Here's a check-in on the Premier League, seven weeks into the season.1. Manchester City (+1)Manchester City will only get so much credit for a lopsided win over Ipswich Town but they rise to the top because they boast a notable lead over Arsenal, who were the team to beat at the start of the campaign.
2. Arsenal (-1)Arsenal were not their most dominant selves in a narrow win over Nottingham Forest but they also went with a rotated team and their depth handled the challenge well enough.3. Brighton and Hove Albion (+1)There are some reasonable caveats to make seven games into the season but Brighton have excelled on multiple occasions already this campaign, Sunday's 5-0 win over Crystal Palace included, and have earned their high ranking here, without a doubt.4. Liverpool (+1)Liverpool benefited from a red card in their win over Brentford but even then, they are starting to shake some of the newness out of the system as Andoni Iraola continues his first season in charge.
5. Chelsea (+1)Maybe, just maybe, Chelsea's early-season defensive chaos is behind them. Stiffer tests than Everton await but a relatively straightforward win over the Toffees is not nothing.6. Leeds United (+1)Leeds look like a midtable team but in a league full of them, someone's bound to rise above the rest. Daniel Farke's side have an admirable consistency about them, one that was on display in their draw against Manchester United, which is why they land here.7. Brentford (-4)Brentford have not maintained their surprisingly strong start the way Brighton have but they still feel like one of the stronger midtable teams, even in defeat against Liverpool.
8. Manchester United (+1)Manchester United's underlying statistics indicate that they should be better than 13th place in the standings but the Red Devils seem impressively resigned to mediocrity. When they solve their own problems is anyone's guess.9. Everton (+1)Maybe the fact that they have one whole striker on their roster would be more costly in a different season but in a campaign with strong midtable energy, Everton are comfortably snug here.10. Aston Villa (+9)The thing about that midtable energy is that once you hit this section, there's a little bit of a splitting-hairs feeling. Aston Villa have work to do to dig out of their early season woes but the thing is, they are starting to do it. Expect them to climb up these rankings in the next few weeks before hitting a period of consistency.
11. Bournemouth (+2)Similar to Villa, it may have taken a while for Bournemouth to pick up their first win but their underlying statistics indicate that they are on course for a steady first season under Marco Rose.12. Sunderland (-4)Some of Sunderland's early season results might come in handy over the course of a long campaign and there's no shame in losing to Bournemouth but it's time to keep an eye on the Black Cats, who really could go in either direction from here.13. Fulham (+4)This is really where the splitting hairs action begins because it feels like as many as eight teams are bad enough to be in the relegation mix right now, Fulham included. The Cottagers sit above the rest for the time being, though, because they actually won their first game this season.
14. Ipswich Town (-2)Being on the wrong side of a thrashing by Manchester City is not actually indicative of Ipswich Town's overall qualities but it's officially time to ask if they can sustain the momentum of their overperformance to start the season.15. Nottingham Forest (-4)Nottingham Forest held their own against Arsenal despite defeat and the underlying numbers suggest that Oliver Glasner's side are better than the results suggest. Five points from seven games is troubling, though there is still time to correct course this season.16. Hull City (-1)Reality might finally be setting in for Hull City, who rode their luck in the Championship last season and continued to do so at the start of this campaign. A drab defeat to Fulham is not a sign of strength, even if their early results serve as a cushion for now.
17. Newcastle United (-3)There are not a lot of redeeming qualities to speak of for Newcastle United, who are learning the hard way that selling all your top players can prove costly, a loss to Villa the latest example.18. Tottenham Hotspur (+2)Tottenham Hotspur are the last winless team in the league and could change that on Monday against Coventry City. If last week's draw against Manchester United is indicative of anything, they could race up the chart like Villa and Bournemouth did, but time will tell if they can actually turn things around.19. Coventry City (-1)Unlike Hull and Ipswich, Coventry are the quintessential promotion side, struggling to cope with the demands of the Premier League in just about every way. They should look at Monday's game against Spurs as a winnable one but that alone will not take them out of the relegation race.
20. Crystal Palace (-4)Crystal Palace are not in the drop zone right now but they were pummeled by Brighton and rank dead last in the Premier League on expected goal differential. Feels like a long season's ahead, whether they like it or not.

title: Military service member dies after fall from Alamodome rafters before UTSA game - CBS Sports
description: An airman died after sustaining injuries during a pre-game exercise
body:
An airman died after sustaining injuries during a pre-game exercise
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
A military service member has died following injuries sustained after falling from the rafters prior to Saturday's college football game between UTSA and Navy inside the Alamodome in San Antonio, Nellis Air Force Base Public Affairs confirmed Sunday.A spokesperson for Nellis Air Force Base said a service member assigned to the 6th Combat Training Squadron, Detachment 2 succumbed to injuries at a local hospital after falling during a pregame rappelling demonstration in connection with UTSA's Salute to Armed Forces & Veterans game.According to the San Antonio Express-News, one of four service members slipped down the rope from the rafters in "an uncontrolled manner" and crashed to the ground. The injured airman was quickly attended to by medical personnel. and put on a stretcher before being taken to a local hospital by the San Antonio Fire Department.The name of the deceased has not been released by the Air Force.The 6th Combat Training Squadron, Detachment 2, is an Air Force unit that supports training for tactical air controllers. The American Conference issued a statement on the incident Sunday."All of us at the American Conference are heartbroken by the death of the U.S. Air Force service member who took part in the pregame demonstration at the Alamodome on Oct. 17," the statement read. "We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, teammates and members of the 57th Wing who had the privilege of serving with him. We honor his service and join the military community in mourning his loss."
The start of Saturday's game was temporarily delayed following the pregame event. American commissioner Tim Pernetti met with members from both UTSA and Navy, Alamodome management officials and local authorities to determine the next steps."At the time of those discussions, Nellis Air Force Base Public Affairs had not publicly confirmed the service member's condition," the American's statement read.UTSA coach Jeff Traylor kept his team in the locker room while the airman was being treated by medical personnel."The only information I had was there had been an incident, and the game was going to be delayed, and we didn't expand upon it any further than that," Traylor said after the game. "I didn't know if I did the right thing or not. I didn't know anything. I didn't know what to tell them, so that's how I handled it."Traylor said his players "could just tell the energy was gone" after coming back onto the field for the opening kickoff in what was a somber environment."Just thinking thoughts and prayers with that family," UTSA quarterback Owen McCown said postgame. "I know we said a prayer postgame, but they'll continue being our thoughts and prayers, and really thinking about them."UTSA beat Navy, 38-34, in front of a crowd of 23,297."It's hard. I just think as players too, my thoughts go immediately with the family," McCown said. "It's obviously bigger than football. And then as just the game went on, kind of got the ebbs and flows, and getting back to playing football. And I thought at first, it was hard to get around, and then finally got going again."
